name: UpCloud
tagline: Finnish cloud VPS hosting built on MaxIOPS all-flash storage performance
description: UpCloud is a Finnish cloud VPS provider built for developers, offering MaxIOPS all-flash storage, hourly or monthly billing and data centers across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
about: UpCloud is a cloud infrastructure provider founded in Helsinki, Finland, aimed at developers and businesses who want to provision and manage cloud servers (VPS) directly rather than through a bundled shared-hosting stack. There is no cPanel or hPanel-style control panel included by default — server management happens through UpCloud's own web console, a CLI, Terraform provider, or its API, which makes it a better fit for technical users comfortable configuring their own stack than for someone wanting a one-click WordPress install.

The entry-level Developer cloud server starts at $5/month for 1 vCPU, 1GB RAM and 25GB of MaxIOPS storage — UpCloud's proprietary all-flash, clustered storage architecture that the company advertises as capable of roughly 100,000 read IOPS, several times faster than standard cloud SSD storage. A separate, cheaper Starter line begins around €3/month but uses standard SSD storage and older-generation CPUs rather than MaxIOPS, so the storage-performance pitch specifically applies to the MaxIOPS-tier plans, not the absolute cheapest option on the site.

Billing is usage-based: server pricing is calculated hourly and capped at the monthly rate, so a server that only runs part of a month costs less than the full monthly price, while running it continuously costs no more than the advertised monthly figure. UpCloud operates data centers across Europe (including Helsinki, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Madrid, Warsaw and Stavanger), the Americas (Chicago, New York, San Jose) and Asia-Pacific (Singapore, Sydney), giving a wider geographic footprint than many budget VPS competitors.
policies: New accounts can try UpCloud with a free trial period before committing to a paid plan; check the current trial length and credit amount on UpCloud's own signup page, as trial terms are adjusted periodically.

Because billing is hourly/usage-based rather than a fixed prepaid term, there isn't a traditional multi-day money-back guarantee the way many shared-hosting companies offer — you're only charged for the hours a server actually runs, so review UpCloud's current billing and refund terms directly before making a purchase decision.
